thread:
incident-bot: ALERT P1 — sudden spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts on prod-apigw (region-us-west). Paging on-call: @alex @jamie. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/apigw/overview (top panel showing 5xx rate + 429s).

alex: oncall, ack. I see a ton of 502/504s and a concurrent 429 surge. Customers reporting slow or missing responses.

jamie: attaching quick snapshot from the last 5m — ingress latency + 5xx graph. 429s jump right before 5xx spike. Feels like backpressure from rate-limiter -> upstream overload.

sara: looking at rate-limit service logs now. tail /var/logs/ratelimit/service.log | grep -E "token_bucket|drop_count"

sara: paste of relevant lines:
```
2026-09-12T06:11:23Z INFO config.push user=natalie pr=gh#2431 set default_rate=10
2026-09-12T06:12:01Z WARN rate_limit dropped=1187 key=global_tokenbucket reason=overflow
2026-09-12T06:12:04Z ERROR upstream request failed status=504 backend=model-router err="context deadline exceeded"
```

luis: wait — PR 2431 was the experimental per-tenant default throttle. I approved it for a canary yesterday but it looks like it rolled out to global default by mistake. That default of 10r/s is way too low.

alex: that explains 429s. If the limiter starts rejecting a bunch of requests, clients probably retry en masse and overwhelm upstream, turning retries into 5xx. Classic backpressure loop.

natalie: I'm on it. Reverting the config now — running `rl-config revert --from=production --to=pre-2431`

ops-bot: deploy-started user=natalie component=ratelimit-service target=production

natalie: rollback applied. Confirming new config: `rl-config get active | grep default_rate` -> shows `default_rate=1000` (expected).

ops-bot: deploy-succeeded user=natalie component=ratelimit-service target=production duration=32s

jamie: after rollback, 429s dropped ~80% within two minutes. 5xx rate also trending down but still above normal. Some upstream backlogs remain.

sara: I'm opening temporary mitigation: increase upstream request timeout and enable slow-path routing for clients failing auth to reduce pressure on main model routers. Commands: 
```
# increase timeout on model-router pool
kubectl patch deployment model-router -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"router","env":[{"name":"UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS","value":"8000"}]}]}}}}'
```

luis: also enabling circuit-breaker to short-circuit heavy retrying clients to 503 quickly instead of letting them pile up. patch applied.

alex: good. notifying affected customers: sales/success — @natalie, can you coordinate outreach for the top 5 paying tenants in US? We should give a short summary + ETA.

natalie: on it. Draft message: "We observed elevated error rates and timeouts earlier this morning due to an internal rate-limit config deployment. We've reverted the change and applied mitigations; service is recovering. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Will share soon.

jamie: quick checklist for rest of mitigation:
- ensure no other config pushes in the last 30m (sara)
- verify queue lengths on model-router (alex)
- keep circuit-breakers in place for 1 hour (luis)
- create incident page + severity timeline (ops-bot)

sara: checked config history — only PR 2431 changed the global default. No other pushes.

alex: queue lengths ok but slow drain — added temporary extra worker pool (scale +2) to model-router: `kubectl scale deployment/model-router --replicas=6 -n prod`

ops-bot: incident-page-created url=https://incidents.redwood/1976543210 owner=alex severity=P1 start_ts=1976543210

luis: monitoring tail: backend latency now dropping; 5xx trending toward baseline in last 10m. Still watching.

natalie: customer comms sent to top 5; SRE + support on standby for follow ups.

alex: handing off ongoing monitoring and post-incident actions to luis (next 8h). I'll be reachable but off-call.

luis: taking ownership. Next steps I’ll lead:
- confirm rollback instrumentation to prevent global rollouts of canary policies
- add a validation gate in ratelimit CI to require explicit scope for defaults (canary vs global)
- run a runbook to test safe rollout path (dev->canary->region).

sara: adding quick rollback-proof in config service: require an explicit `--global` flag and add a 5 minute hold before global flips. I'll open a PR and tag alex/natalie for review.

ops-bot: handoff note created incident=1976543210 new_owner=luis

natalie: postmortem owner assigned: natalie. ETA for draft: EOD today.

alex: closing the page once postmortem is attached. Great work everyone. If anything changes ping here, otherwise this thread will serve as the timeline. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status=resolved (degraded -> recovery) reason=reverted-rate-config mitigations=rollback,scale-up,timeout-increase,circuit-breaker first_detected=1976543210 resolved_at=1976543442

luis: noting action items (will create JIRA): RL-451 revert-protection, RL-452 config-validation, OPS-123 backlog drain automation.

natalie: thanks. I'll publish customer-facing note after postmortem review.

alex: nice quick mitigation. Handing off fully to luis.

luis: thanks team — monitoring for next hour then I'll transition to follow-ups.
